turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr Menon, please sit. I am sorry you waited. The nurse has already put a note on the file. What brought you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The knee. Left knee is paining, and there is this wretched fitness form from the office. I am tired, doctor, can we finish fast.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I am Padma, his wife. We came for the knee and that form only. Outside, the sister checked the BP and made a face, she said it is high, show the doctor.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): She makes a face for everything. In the clinic it shoots up, it is white coat, that is all. At home it is perfectly normal.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will come to the BP, I have not forgotten. Knee first, so I don't miss why you actually came. Which knee, and what does the pain feel like?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Left. Inner side, a dull pain, more when I climb the stairs in the flat. Sitting in accounts the whole day does not help either.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Diwali, or after Diwali. I cannot date it, last winter or the one before, something like that. Don't pin me to a day.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It is three months, doctor. After Onam he started, not Diwali. He is mixing the festivals because he is irritable today.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not mixing. I said I do not know the date, and it is paining now. Kindly don't speak for me.

[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Left knee pain is present, worse on stairs, and you cannot date the start, Diwali or after or last winter, while your wife says three months from after Onam. I will hold it as roughly two to three months, and that is not agreed by both of you.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Hold whatever you like. I just want the knee looked at and that form done.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it swell, lock, or give way? Any limp?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling. It does not lock and it does not give way. I am not limping, I walk.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Evening time the left knee swells, I have seen it myself. And from the bus stop he limps, whether he admits or not.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not swollen, and I do not limp. After sitting it feels tight, that is different. She adds extra.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you deny swelling and a limp, and she reports both. I will check the joint myself. The tightness after sitting I have heard from you.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And giddiness, doctor, two weeks now. He held the kitchen wall, I saw it with my own eyes.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not giddiness. I was tired, the current had gone, and I did not hold any wall. Stop adding things.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Giddiness stays disputed, I will not treat it as fact. You do accept that you are tired?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I am tired. Whole day in the office and then this running around. Tired is not giddy.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): And breathlessness on the stairs?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I am slow because of the knee, that is all.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not record breathlessness from that. Any headache?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. Leave the headache. I did not come for that.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not put headache down either. Any operation on this knee before?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never. No surgery on the knee.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diabetes, thyroid, any heart problem we should know about?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar is normal, they checked. Thyroid no. No heart problem.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): At the company camp they said his cholesterol was borderline. He never collected the paper, so don't ask him for a number.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): They said borderline, yes. Last winter, or the one before, I can't say which. I don't remember any figure.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): An old cholesterol test, told to you as borderline only, no figure, and you cannot date which winter. I will not take that as confirmed high cholesterol.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. I don't want a new tablet for a word like borderline.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you actually taking now? Any BP tablet?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No BP tablet, nothing regular.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last time some doctor gave amlodipine. Five milligram, I think. He will say he didn't, but the strip was in the cupboard.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not denying the name. Maybe five milligram, I am not sure of the dose. I took it a few days, my head felt heavy, I stopped, and I am not taking it now.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): So amlodipine was started and then stopped, and the dose is only a maybe, not a current medicine. Any allergy to any drug?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergy. Nothing happens with medicines.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): And for the knee pain, any tablet you take?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin. I was going to say two tablets, no, it is one tablet of five hundred milligrams, when the pain is more. Not every day.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol 500 mg by mouth, as needed for the knee, which you already use. I am not starting any BP tablet today.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. That is what I wanted to hear, almost.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His father had a stroke, I should say it. Around sixty-eight. It sits in my mind whenever BP comes up.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, my father had a stroke, that is an old story. I am fifty-nine, I am not him. Can we move to the knee.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Father, a stroke, noted as family history. It is not a reason to start you on treatment in this chair today.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are still in the accounts job, sitting through the day?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, same company, twenty years, sitting only. I live with her, and walking to the bus is my exercise, there is no gym.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or take alcohol?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Smoke, mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really, one at a wedding is not smoking. Alcohol is a small peg at functions, not regular. Leave both, please.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not list you as a smoker on that answer. Let me examine the knee.

[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left knee, the skin looks normal, and I cannot feel any swelling or fluid. The inner joint line is tender when I press, you bend and straighten fully, and there is a little crepitus on bending.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, that spot, yes, that is where it pains. Don't press again, I am already irritated.
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry. I will listen to the chest because the pressure outside was high. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur, lungs are clear, and the pulse is 82, regular.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Then the sister was making a big scene for nothing. I told you it is clinic BP.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Her first reading, written on the slip, is 168 over 102. I am taking a second one myself now that you have been sitting.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): This second reading is 154 over 94. It is lower, still raised, and it is not the same number.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): See, itself it is coming down. White coat only. At home, on the neighbour's machine, it was one-twenty something, last week or the week before, I forget which.
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He did it once, standing in their hall and talking the whole time. I don't believe that one-twenty. He will not sit quiet for anybody.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): It was normal, I am telling you. I know my own body better than the two of you.

[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): The clinic readings were 168 over 102 and then 154 over 94, and they don't match each other. You call it white coat, the home check is vaguely one-twenty with the date unclear, and your wife does not trust how it was taken. I cannot decide today if this is white coat or a sustained high BP.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): So no tablet. Say it in plain words.

[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): No tablet started today. We will arrange home monitoring, morning and night, sitting, for seven days, both numbers in a diary, and I will have the desk issue you the clinic monitor.
[SEG0066] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will write the numbers down. If I leave it to him he will forget half the days.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): I will not forget. She can write if she wants, but it is my BP, not a school project.
[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): Same method each time, please. No tea just before, cuff arm at heart level, back supported. Bring that sheet with you.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): And my form? If I go back with no signature, HR will eat my head.

[SEG0070] person_1 (DOCTOR): I cannot sign the fitness form as a normal BP today, so bring the same form to the review. For the knee, my working impression is early wear and tear, osteoarthritis of the left knee, and it is provisional only.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): Wear and tear at fifty-nine, wonderful. What to do.

[SEG0072] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it has not settled when I see you next, we might do an x-ray of the left knee, not today. Meanwhile avoid deep squatting, use ice in the evening if it feels tight, and continue the Crocin you already take when the pain is bad.
[SEG0073] person_3 (CAREGIVER): If the home readings are also high, then what? I need to know, he will ask me in the car.

[SEG0074] person_1 (DOCTOR): If most of the home readings sit above 140 over 90, we discuss a tablet at the review, only if. It may be white coat hypertension, or it may be true hypertension, and both stay open.
[SEG0075] person_2 (PATIENT): Review when? Don't say one month, the office will not wait.
[SEG0076] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks, with the diary and the form. That visit is planned, not only if you feel like coming.
[SEG0077] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Fine. I am fed up of clinics, but fine.
[SEG0078] person_1 (DOCTOR): If chest pain comes, or true severe giddiness, or the knee locks and you cannot walk, do not wait for that date. Otherwise it is two weeks.
[SEG0079] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will bring him, thank you doctor. He did not sleep well last night, the neighbour's dog was at it, that is why the temper.
[SEG0080] person_2 (PATIENT): I slept badly, yes. The dog is not a medical case, and I am irritable because this is taking so long, not because of her dog story.
[SEG0081] person_1 (DOCTOR): Poor sleep last night, noted, and you are tired and irritable today. Let me repeat the plan once so nothing stays fuzzy.

[SEG0082] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left knee pain, with the onset date uncertain and the duration not agreed, so about two to three months unconfirmed. On examination there was no swelling, tiredness is accepted, giddiness is not agreed, there is no chest pain, no drug allergy, and no current BP tablet. Amlodipine was stopped and the dose is uncertain, the cholesterol was only recalled as borderline, and your father had a stroke. The BP was 168 over 102 and then 154 over 94, no new medicine today, home readings for seven days, back in two weeks, an x-ray only if the knee is still bad, and a tablet only if the home readings stay high.
[SEG0083] person_2 (PATIENT): You have said the whole thing twice. I heard you. Can we go now, the car is in the sun.

spec.situation: Patient attends for something minor (a knee or a form) and the nurse finds high BP; BP read aloud twice with different numbers; patient says it is white coat; family history of stroke said in passing; no tablets started today, home monitoring arranged.
features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Pain, dull, left knee, stairs supported; duration/certainty not certain because onset and 2-3 months were disputed.
bad.text: dull left knee pain on stairs (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, duration=approximately 2 to 3 months, temporality=current, body_site=left knee, aggravating_factors=climbing stairs, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Amlodipine discontinued after a few days supported; 5 mg dose was only a maybe, not confirmed.
bad.text: amlodipine (dose=5 mg, duration=a few days, indication=blood pressure, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Completed cholesterol test supported, but it was from company camp, not requested by patient.

omissions.text: Negative finding missing: patient denied any current limp ('I am not limping, I walk').
Negative finding missing: patient denied knee swelling when specifically asked ('No swelling'). This is clinically relevant alongside the caregiver's disputed report of evening swelling.
Negative finding missing: breathlessness on stairs was asked and not recorded because the patient's answer was equivocal and insufficient ('Sometimes, not really... I am slow because of the knee').
Negative finding missing: headache was asked and not recorded because the patient's answer was equivocal and insufficient ('sometimes, not really').
History omission: patient stated he is not taking any regular medicines and specifically no current BP tablet ('No. No BP tablet, nothing regular').
Medication detail recorded wrongly: amlodipine 5 mg was not confirmed; the dose was only 'maybe five milligram'/'I am not sure of the dose'. Recording it as a definite 5 mg is inaccurate.

Investigation/history detail recorded wrongly: prior cholesterol test was from a company camp and was only reported as 'borderline'; the doctor explicitly did not accept this as confirmed high cholesterol. Recording it simply as a completed cholesterol test requested by the patient is inaccurate.
Examination finding missing: pulse was regular (82, regular), not just 82 bpm.
